title: rollforward-rescue-notes-image-digest-pin
content:
Context:
- Canary 2024-11-02 03:20 UTC failed during a small traffic shift (10% -> 50%) for service `vector-embedder` on cluster prod-us-east. Symptoms: elevated 5xxs from canary pods, readiness flapping, downstream timeouts.
- This doc is my scratchpad for troubleshooting + minimal rollforward steps (prefer rollforward/pin to rollback where safe).

Initial hypothesis (fast): image tag drift / ephemeral tagging from CI produced different content than expected (same semver, different digest). Canary got a newer digest that regressed.

What I checked (commands & outputs captured):
- k8s: list the canary replicasets/pods\  > kubectl -n prod get deploy vector-embedder -o wide\  NAME                 READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE\  vector-embedder     8/10    2            1           4d\  -> Observed 2 new replicas (canary).
\- describe failing pod (short excerpts)\  > kubectl -n prod describe pod vector-embedder-5f6c9b7d8-xyz\  Events:\    Type     Reason     Age   From               Message\    ----     ------     ----  ----               -------\    Warning  Unhealthy  2m    kubelet            Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
\- pod logs (app container):\  > kubectl -n prod logs vector-embedder-5f6c9b7d8-xyz --tail=80\  2024-11-02T03:25:12Z ERROR inference: model load failed: checksum mismatch for shard 3\  2024-11-02T03:25:12Z WARN  server: warmup incomplete, returning 503
\- image info: check deployed container image (digest vs tag)\  > kubectl -n prod get pod vector-embedder-5f6c9b7d8-xyz -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}'\  gcr.io/rw-inference/vector-embedder:2024.11.01\  > crane digest gcr.io/rw-inference/vector-embedder:2024.11.01\  sha256:aa11b2c4c6f7b1e4f9a9c3d1d0a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1aa
- CI release artifact registry shows multiple pushes under same tag 2024.11.01 within 30m window -> replication/overwrite policy in pipeline.
- Verified the healthy stable pods are running a different digest:\  > kubectl -n prod get pod vector-embedder-78d4a2b3-abc -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}'\  gcr.io/rw-inference/vector-embedder:2024.11.01@sha256:cc33d4e5...
  -> stable digest cc33d4e5... vs canary digest aa11b2c4... -> confirms tag reused.

Immediate decision: avoid full rollback (which would flip a lot of traffic) — instead rollforward the canary to the known-good digest (pin digest) and resume.

Commands I executed to pin the canary (recording exact commands used):
- kubectl set image with digest\  > kubectl -n prod set image deployment/vector-embedder vector-embedder=gcr.io/rw-inference/vector-embedder@sha256:cc33d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8g9h0i1j2k3l4m5n6 --record\  deployment.apps/vector-embedder image updated
- verify rollout status\  > kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/vector-embedder\  waiting for deployment "vector-embedder" rollout to finish: 1 of 10 updated replicas are available\  -> watched until new pods ready, readiness stabilized.
- confirm updated pods pulled digest\  > kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=vector-embedder -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.spec.containers[0].image}\n'\  vector-embedder-...:gcr.io/rw-inference/vector-embedder@sha256:cc33d4e5f6a7...

Result: within 4 minutes after pinning digest, 5xxs dropped back to baseline and canary health indicators green. Traffic ramp resumed to 50% and then 100% per rollout policy.

Root-cause evidence (notes to include in postmortem):\- CI pipeline allowed mutable tags (pipeline step `docker push --tag`) without immutably pinning tag->digest mapping or teaching the deploy pipeline to use digest.\- artifact registry accepted two different images with same tag (overwrite) during a CI re-run; no blocking on content-diff or digest check during promotion.\- deploy tooling used tag-only in helm values (image.tag=2024.11.01) and didn't read digest in the values file.

Short-term mitigation applied (actions taken):
1) Pin digest for canary via kubectl set image (above) and monitor for 30m.
2) Opened PR to helm chart values to include optional `image.digest` and prefer `image.digest` over `image.tag` when present (see linked PR).
3) Added a temporary job that verifies image digest of the tag in GCR matches the digest used during CI build and refuses to promote if mismatch.

Longer-term changes to propose (to include in postmortem):
- CI: change release pipeline to publish and promote artifacts by digest; tag should be metadata only (ci should fail if tag reused).
- Deploy tooling (helm/flux/argo): allow explicit digest pinning and prefer digest in manifests. Add validation webhook that checks that tag->digest mapping hasn't changed since promotion timestamp.
- Create monitoring alert for any rolling update where the new replicaset's image digest != stable digest for the tag (heuristic to catch mutable-tag pushes).

Rollforward vs rollback decision notes (why rollforward here):
- Rollback would have moved all traffic back to old revision but stable pods already had the good digest; rollback would have been unnecessary and slower.\- Pinning digest (rollforward to known-good image) is lower blast radius and faster for this class of regression.

Commands/snippets to include in runbook (condensed):
- Check image digests for tag: `crane digest gcr.io/...:TAG` or `gcloud container images describe --format='get(image_summary.fully_qualified_digest)'`\- Get pod image: `kubectl get pod -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}'`\- Pin deployment to digest: `kubectl -n $NS set image deploy/$DEP $CNAME=$IMAGE@sha256:$DIGEST --record`\- Helm: `helm upgrade --reuse-values --set image.digest=sha256:... myrelease ./charts/vector-embedder` (chart must support image.digest)

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-ups):
- Who retriggered the CI push that reused tag 2024.11.01 within the release window? (audit CI history)\- Add an automated gate: prevent tagging if registry already has same tag but different digest (or require `--force` with human approval).\- Investigate artifact registry retention / replication latencies between regions that might cause clients to pull an earlier digest after a rewrite.

Post-incident quick checklist (for me next time):
- Grab: `kubectl get rs -n $NS -o wide` and `kubectl get pods -n $NS -l app=$APP -o wide`\- Check: pod logs + readiness errors (grep for "checksum" or "model load" for inference services)\- Determine: stable vs canary digest difference (`kubectl get pod -o jsonpath` on each)\- Mitigate: prefer pin to known-good digest; resume rollout slowly and watch SLOs\- Followup: open change in CI to push digests + update charts

Notes to add to postmortem timeline (timestamps localize to UTC):\- 03:12 - CI triggered release (tag 2024.11.01 created)\- 03:20 - Canary started receiving traffic shift\- 03:25 - 5xx spike observed, SRE paging triggered\- 03:30 - confirmed digest mismatch between canary & stable\- 03:34 - pinned digest to known-good cc33d4e5...\- 03:40 - canary stabilized, ramp resumed, incident resolved 03:50

Misc artifacts to attach to postmortem: helm history output, kube describe of failing pod, logs showing checksum mismatch, CI job run IDs that pushed both digests.

Personal notes: keep this file lightweight. If we repeat this class of bug one more time without CI+deploy changes, escalate to mandatory digest-only promotion policy.

End of scratchpad.
